atlas-nz.0001: A small market with a generous permit: a degree studied full-time in New Zealand for at least 30 weeks can lead to a post-study work visa of up to three years. Auckland is the commercial centre, producing 37% of the country’s output in finance and insurance from its city centre alone.

atlas-nz.0008: New Zealand was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-nz.0009: No source read gives graduate outcomes or entry pay for international master’s graduates in New Zealand.
atlas-nz.0010: How long the post-study work visa lasts for each kind of master’s is not set out on the page read.
atlas-nz.0011: Income tax runs from 10.5% on the first NZ$15,600 through 17.5%, 30% and 33% to 39% on income over NZ$180,000 (rates from 1 April 2025).
atlas-nz.0012: Auckland’s city centre, the country’s commercial hub, produces 37% of New Zealand’s GDP in financial and insurance services and 28% in information media and telecommunications; nearly 40 of the country’s top 200 tech firms are in or around it.
atlas-nz.0013: Auckland employs 34% of New Zealand’s workers (early 2025); financial and insurance services employed 42,200 people there in 2024, up from 40,900.
atlas-nz.0014: The capital, for government, professional services and finance
atlas-nz.0016: The South Island’s main city and Canterbury’s centre
atlas-nz.0019: A Wellington regional-council report lists the region’s five largest industries by GDP as professional, scientific and technical services, public administration and safety, financial and insurance services, health care, and information media and telecommunications.
atlas-nz.0020: Canterbury is New Zealand’s second-largest manufacturing region, with 14% of the country’s manufacturing GDP; manufacturing employs 40,000 people there, about 10% of the region’s jobs.
atlas-nz.0021: Wellington’s finance and Christchurch’s business roles are not rated: the sources read rank industries by output, not graduate jobs by role, and the Wellington report dates from 2020; Kiwibank, the Reserve Bank and Air New Zealand were not read.
atlas-nz.0022: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts Auckland in the 31–40 range of its emerging ecosystems, the biggest climb in that top 40 (more than 75 places).
atlas-nz.0023: Startup Genome’s 2026 page for Wellington gives no rank; it puts the ecosystem’s value at $2 billion, against a regional average of $5.6 billion, and total early-stage funding at $87 million, against a regional average of $202 million.
atlas-nz.0024: ANZ’s New Zealand holding company has its registered office and principal place of business at ANZ Centre, 23–29 Albert Street, Auckland.
atlas-nz.0025: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, founded in New Zealand in 1969, gives an Auckland address and says it employs over 7,500 people around the world, more than 950 of them in research and development.
atlas-nz.0026: Xero’s registered address is 19–23 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington.
atlas-nz.0027: At 30 June 2025, 42.6% of the Public Service workforce was in the Wellington region, 21.3% in Auckland and 10.3% in Canterbury.
atlas-nz.0028: ChristchurchNZ says the city’s tech sector contributes $2.4 billion of GDP and over 15,000 jobs, and names Tait Communications and Seequent as pioneering global businesses based there.
atlas-nz.0029: No regional pay was found: Stats NZ publishes earnings by region only through its data explorer, which could not be read, so the pay metric is left out; rent is left out because no citable rent source was available and the official rental-bond data are by area unit, not one-bedroom flats by city.
atlas-nz.0030: The Public Service share of Wellington (42.6%) is a share of the workforce, not a headcount; its standing as management is a judgement (public administration read as management).
atlas-nz.0031: Graduate recruitment in New Zealand runs in English: Deloitte’s stages are a cover letter, a one-way video interview and a face-to-face interview, and an accredited employer work visa for skill levels 3 to 5 requires proof of English.
atlas-nz.0032: The main graduate cohort starts in February: Deloitte’s graduate roles start on 22 February 2027 and its summer internship ran from 16 November 2026 to 12 February 2027; NZ Government Procurement took applications from 17 July to 17 August 2026, and the University of Auckland’s Internship and Graduate expo was on 29 July 2026.
atlas-nz.0033: New Zealand’s unemployment rate was 5.6% in the June 2026 quarter, up from 5.4% in March, and the underutilisation rate of 15 to 24-year-olds rose from 33.6% to 37.0% over the year; 77% of graduate employers filled some or all graduate roles from people who had already worked for them.
atlas-nz.0034: principal place of business on Albert Street
atlas-nz.0035: over 7,500 staff worldwide, with an Auckland address
atlas-nz.0038: Tech employers, among them Tait Communications and Seequent
atlas-nz.0040: New Zealand employers fill graduate roles largely from people who have already worked for them: 77% of employers in the graduate employers’ survey filled some or all of their graduate roles with candidates who had done work experience with them.
atlas-nz.0041: Word of mouth is one of the channels graduates name as most common and effective, and friends and family influence the job decisions of over two thirds of graduates.
atlas-nz.0043: In the 2025 surveys, 63% of graduates had worked for their current employer before starting their graduate role, 86% gained industry-relevant work experience during their studies, and 83% of interns want a permanent role with their internship employer.
atlas-nz.0044: Deloitte’s summer internship is for students in their penultimate year and ran from 16 November 2026 to 12 February 2027; its graduate roles start on 22 February 2027. Tahatū, the government careers site, advises starting to look for an internship 6 to 9 months ahead.
atlas-nz.0045: Competition is also at intern level: 30% of interns submitted eight or more internship applications.
atlas-nz.0046: 92% of employers in the 2025 survey have a formal graduate development programme, and 46% spend more than NZ$30,000 on graduate training and development.
atlas-nz.0047: The Big Four and mid-tier firms recruit for a February start: Deloitte takes people finishing their studies or within the previous 24 months, from all majors, and Baker Tilly Staples Rodway advertised 20 to 25 places at NZ$50,000 to 60,000 with February or July starts.
atlas-nz.0048: Employers do not all open at once: the NZ Government Procurement programme took applications from 17 July to 17 August 2026 for a February 2027 start, and Suncorp New Zealand closed most streams on 31 August for a January start.
atlas-nz.0050: Word of mouth ranks with employer websites, careers expos and LinkedIn as the most common and effective channels for graduates, and for interns word of mouth comes first; friends and family influence over two thirds of graduates and 65% of interns.
atlas-nz.0051: Tahatū says many jobs are not advertised, so contacting employers directly is worthwhile, and it names networking as one of the best ways to get a job.
atlas-nz.0053: Careers expos are among the channels graduates and interns use most. The University of Auckland ran a Business and Law expo on 12 March 2026 and an Internship and Graduate expo for all faculties on 29 July 2026.
atlas-nz.0054: Firms also come to campuses: the University of Waikato hosted a networking event with PwC, KPMG, Deloitte and EY on 13 March 2024, and Summer of Tech links tech employers with students and graduates through about 100 events a year.
atlas-nz.0055: Public Service graduate programmes and internships
atlas-nz.0056: NZ Government Jobs lists Public Service vacancies with “Graduate” and “Internship” categories; Tahatū says the government runs internships in the public service, some for students or recent graduates, and points to the Public Service Commission page on graduate programmes.
atlas-nz.0057: The NZ Government Procurement Graduate Programme took 10 graduates for two years, with four six-month placements across agencies in Auckland and Wellington.
atlas-nz.0059: Employer websites head the channels graduates name, and experienced hires apply the same way or through boards and recruiters: Trade Me Jobs showed 8,880 jobs nationwide on the day it was read, and Tahatū lists recruitment agencies and job boards as sources of vacancies.
atlas-nz.0060: Applications for the main graduate cohort cluster in the year before a February start: Deloitte’s graduate roles start on 22 February 2027 and it also lets students finishing mid-year join that national cohort; NZ Government Procurement applied from 17 July to 17 August 2026 for February 2027.
atlas-nz.0061: Summer internships fill the Southern Hemisphere break: Deloitte’s ran from 16 November 2026 to 12 February 2027, and Summer of Tech opens candidate registration for its 2027 programme in January.
atlas-nz.0062: The market is crowded: 60% of employers saw more graduate applications in 2025, 13% of them by more than 50%, and 41% of graduates received two or more offers.
atlas-nz.0063: The Big Four recruit through campus events at the universities, and mid-tier firms run graduate programmes too: Baker Tilly Staples Rodway advertised 20 to 25 places at NZ$50,000 to 60,000, with February or July starts.
atlas-nz.0064: Deloitte takes all majors, but Audit, Assurance and Reporting Advisory need prerequisite papers, or bridging papers completed before starting CPA or Chartered Accountants ANZ studies.
